text:
priya: Heads-up — planning a short sync to pin down acceptance criteria and metrics for the long-term segmentation/routing roadmap. Want to surface customer asks that must block GA and what can wait for phase 2.

sam: +1. Can we capture: SLA floors, migration blast radius, rollback story, and any billing/pricing constraints?

anya: Also add usability: admin UX for tenant slices, and clarity on which policies are editable by customers vs platform. Customers keep asking for an easy revert.

mike: From eng: we need precise perf targets (p95 p99), and headroom for burst traffic. If we don't define, infra will under/overprovision.

priya: Agreed. Drafting a short acceptance checklist now — will paste. Hoping to keep this thread lightweight so we can convert to an RFC later.

kate: Related ask from AE: named customers require cross-region affinity + data residency opt-in. That shapes routing templates.

priya: Here's the initial checklist — feedback welcome:
```
- SLA: 99.95% availability for Dedicated customers on routed traffic
- Latency: median < 50ms, p95 < 200ms for regional-local requests
- Isolation: noisy-tenant throttling + soft-eviction path tested
- Migration: canary rollout w/ automated rollback on error spikes
- Billing: clear pricing tiers for affinity/reserved lanes vs burst routing
- UX: admin page to pin/unpin tenants and view affected routes
- Privacy: region tag + KMS scoping for Private deployments
```

sam: Looks solid. Suggest adding a measurable quality metric for model output regression during routing switches (e.g., key prompts eval set).

anya: +1 on eval set. Also we should call out the minimum telemetry: per-tenant token rate, route failovers, fallback counts.

mike: Ops note: need a migration playbook stub — prechecks, cutover window, abort criteria. I can draft one if ppl agree on rollback triggers.

kate: Customer ask: ability to opt into per-route guarantees (e.g., low-latency lane for chat vs best-effort for batch embeddings). That impacts pricing.

priya: OK — that becomes a product decision: expose per-route QoS in console (and charge accordingly). We'll add to phase 1 if it affects existing deals.

sam: Risk log quick hits: 1) Cross-region data replication costs, 2) Unexpected tail-latency from long KV cache chains, 3) Ambiguous ownership of routing policies across Platform/Product/Infra.

anya: For ownership: propose Policy DSL lives with Platform, but product owns customer facing defaults and guardrails. Document in RFC.

mike: On telemetry: suggest these minimum alerts for rollout safety: error rate > 1% absolute increase, latency p95 increase > 30%, fallback rate > 0.5% per minute.

priya: Noted. For launch gating, propose these gates:
- Technical: automated rollback + canary for 2 region pairs, perf within SLO for 72h
- Operational: runbook + SRE oncall rotation covered
- Legal/Security: data residency checklist for customers in scope
- Sales/Price: any named-customer price commitments documented

kate: Can we add a customer communication template for migration windows? Sales wants a one-pager they can send.

priya: I'll add a short template to the RFC repo.

anya: One more: experiments we should run before GA — 1) synthetic noisy-tenant injection, 2) randomized route failover, 3) model-variant fallback correctness checks.

mike: I'll own the noisy-tenant test harness. Will mock 10 tenants at 10x baseline requests and run through the throttling and eviction path.

sam: Who's owning pricing options for per-route QoS? Product + Finance?

priya: Product + Finance, with input from Sales. Kate, can you help surface the top 3 customers that would buy QoS?

kate: Yep — will share anonymized list by EOD.

kevin-bot: Deploy bot: created temp RFC draft "segmentation-routing-acceptance" (link: https://r.wd/r/seg-route-draft). Please review.

priya: Perfect. Next steps: I'll consolidate checklist + gating into the RFC, tag owners for playbooks/tests. Quick ask — if anyone has a hard blocker (customer deal or regulation) that must be in P1, flag it here within 24h.

sam: No blockers from infra side beyond what's listed.

anya: No blockers from product compliance; will flag if legal has any residency issues after review.

mike: No blockers. Starting test harness work tomorrow.

kate: I'll surface customer asks by EOD.

priya: Thanks all. I'll ping when RFC is ready for review. :v:
